claim: The PR says it proves Ville's inequality, but it does not. Ville's inequality is a maximal inequality, μ {ω | ∃ n, λ ≤ f n ω} ≤ 𝔼[f 0] / λ (or a bound on sup_{k ≤ n} f k). What the PR proves is the bound at one fixed time n: Markov's inequality (`mul_meas_ge_le_integral_of_nonneg`) combined with 𝔼[f n] ≤ 𝔼[f 0], three lines in all. The name would send users who look up Ville's inequality to a weaker statement. `integral_stoppedValue_le` is exactly the ingredient the real maximal proof needs, yet nothing in the file uses it.
requested_change: Either prove the maximal statement or drop the name. The maximal statement would first be the finite-horizon λ·μ{λ ≤ (range (n+1)).sup' … f k} ≤ 𝔼[f 0], using the hitting time `hittingBtwn f {y | λ ≤ y} 0 n` together with `integral_stoppedValue_le`, mirroring `smul_le_stoppedValue_hittingBtwn`/`maximal_ineq`; then the bound over all n by a monotone limit. If that is out of scope, retitle the PR and rename the docstrings so the fixed-time Markov corollary is not called Ville's inequality.
